name: Windsor
ground: A chalk bluff above the Thames, chosen because it is thirty metres higher than everything around it and a day’s march from London. Every other decision here follows from those two facts and nothing follows from taste.

motte.note: Thrown up in the 1070s. The Round Tower sits on it.

keep.name: The Round Tower
keep.note: Round because a round tower has no corner to undermine.

wards.name: Upper Ward
wards.note: The private side. State apartments along the north.

wards.name: Lower Ward
wards.note: The public side. The chapel, and everybody who is not the household.

axis.name: The Long Walk
axis.note: Four and a quarter kilometres, dead straight, and it exists so that the castle is the only thing at the end of it.

figures.value: 15 m of piled chalk, dug from the ditch around it
since the 1070s, which no other castle manages

lesson: It is not symmetrical and was never meant to be. Two wards of different sizes either side of a mound, because the mound came first and everything else went where there was room. A plan like this cannot be designed; it can only be arrived at.
